intent: One labeled control with optional hint and error. Label on top or start (left).
useWhen: Any labeled Input, Textarea, Select, DatePicker, or Switch
When helper text or a validation error sits with the control
doNotUseWhen: Checkbox with its own label and no extra hint/error — use Checkbox
RadioGroup — it provides its own legend
A group of fields with a legend — use FieldSet
Required instructions stay in hint — help is extra explanation, not a substitute

hint.note: helper text. Hidden when error is set.

help.note: Extra explanation. Field puts HelpPopover beside the label (placement right). title is the Field label. content is help. Not a substitute for hint.

labelPosition.note: top stacks. start is horizontal (label left). Hint and error stay under the control.

requirements: Label htmlFor matches child control id
Hint or error id is passed to the child as describedBy
When help is set, HelpPopover sits beside the label; hint and error stay under the control

doNot: Do not invent FieldLabel, FieldContent, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldTitle, FieldGroup, FieldLegend, FieldSeparator, Form, FormField, FormItem, FormControl, or FormMessage
Do not wrap Button or layout components
Do not use start on Field for prefix text — that is Input start
Do not put help on Input, Textarea, Select, or DatePicker — Field owns it
snippet: <Field label="Email" htmlFor="email" hint="We never share your email."><Input id="email" type="email" /></Field>
